section.content: The machine learning method comprises the following steps: processing the first sensing data by the first detector to generate first object data; generating, by a first detector, a first uncertainty fraction of the first object data; processing the second sensing data by a second detector to generate second object data; generating a second uncertainty fraction of the second object data by a second detector; generating first weight data corresponding to the first object data and second weight data corresponding to the second object data according to the first uncertainty fraction and the second uncertainty fraction through a model; generating prediction data at least according to the first and second weight data; and training the model according to the prediction data. The first and second sensing data correspond to the same environment, and the first and second object data correspond to objects in the environment. Thus, the model performs better.

机器学习方法包括：通过第一侦测器处理第一感测数据，以产生第一物件数据；通过第一侦测器产生第一物件数据的第一不确定性分数；通过第二侦测器处理第二感测数据，以产生第二物件数据；通过第二侦测器产生第二物件数据的第二不确定性分数；通过模型，依据第一及第二不确定性分数产生对应第一物件数据的第一权重数据及对应第二物件数据的第二权重数据；至少依据第一及第二权重数据产生预测数据；以及依据预测数据训练模型。第一及第二感测数据对应相同的环境，且第一及第二物件数据对应环境中的物件。如此一来，模型表现较佳。

Machine learning methodTechnical Field

The present disclosure relates to machine learning, and more particularly to a machine learning method.

Background

When training the model, the model tends to make too confident a determination for the object in the adverse context (adverse scenario), i.e., the model easily classifies the object of the non-specific class into the specific class to produce a determination of false positive or leaks the specific object to produce a determination of false negative. In addition, when fusing object data of different sensors, some sensors are highly affected by adverse situations, and the processor equally considers all object data, so that the model performs poorly. Therefore, how to overcome the above-mentioned drawbacks is an important subject in the art.

Disclosure of Invention

The embodiment of the invention comprises a machine learning method. The machine learning method comprises the following steps: processing the first sensing data by the first detector to generate first object data; generating, by a first detector, a first uncertainty fraction of the first object data; processing the second sensed data by a second detector different from the first detector to generate second object data; generating a second uncertainty fraction of the second object data by a second detector; generating first weight data corresponding to the first detector and second weight data corresponding to the second detector according to the first uncertainty fraction and the second uncertainty fraction through the model; generating prediction data at least according to the first weight data and the second weight data; and training the model according to the prediction data. The first sensing data and the second sensing data correspond to the same environment, the first object data corresponds to objects in the environment, and the second object data corresponds to objects.

In some embodiments, generating the prediction data includes: inputting the first object data, the first weight data, the second object data and the second weight data into a fusion network; and generating the prediction data through the converged network.

In some embodiments, generating the first weight data and the second weight data includes: generating first feature data according to at least a portion of the first object data and the first uncertainty fraction through a first expert network; generating second feature data according to the second uncertainty fraction and at least a portion of the second object data via a second expert network; and generating the first weight data and the second weight data according to the first feature data and the second feature data, wherein the first expert network and the second expert network respectively correspond to the first detector and the second detector.

In some embodiments, the first detector and the second detector correspond to a first sensor and a second sensor, respectively, the type of the first sensor is different from the type of the second sensor, the first sensing data corresponds to the data sensed by the first sensor, and the second sensing data corresponds to the data sensed by the second sensor.

In some embodiments, the machine learning method further comprises: processing the third sensing data by the third detector to generate third object data; generating a third uncertainty fraction of the third object data by the third detector, wherein the third sensing data corresponds to the environment and the third object data corresponds to the at least one object.

In some embodiments, generating the first weight data and the second weight data includes: generating third feature data according to at least a portion of the third object data and the third uncertainty fraction via a third expert network; and generating the first weight data and the second weight data according to the first feature data, the second feature data and the third feature data, wherein the first expert network, the second expert network and the third expert network correspond to the first detector, the second detector and the third detector respectively.

In some embodiments, the first detector, the second detector and the third detector respectively correspond to a first sensor, a second sensor and a third sensor, the type of the first sensor, the type of the second sensor and the type of the third sensor are different from each other, the first sensing data corresponds to the data sensed by the first sensor, the second sensing data corresponds to the data sensed by the second sensor, and the third sensing data corresponds to the data sensed by the third sensor.

In some embodiments, generating the prediction data includes: generating third weight data corresponding to the third detector according to the third uncertainty fraction by the model; inputting the first object data, the first weight data, the second object data, the second weight data, the third object data and the third weight data into a fusion network; and generating the prediction data through the converged network.

In some embodiments, generating the first uncertainty score includes: generating a plurality of first object data according to the first sensing data by the first detector; and generating the first uncertainty score according to the distribution of the plurality of first object data, wherein the first uncertainty score is greater when the distribution of the plurality of first object data is wider.

In some embodiments, the first uncertainty score includes an uncertainty score of a confidence score of the at least one object and an uncertainty score of a bounding box of the at least one object, the confidence score corresponding to a probability that the at least one object is assigned to a category by the first detector, and the bounding box corresponding to a location and a volume occupied by the at least one object in the space of the first sensed data.

Detailed Description

It will be further understood that the terms "comprises" and/or "comprising," when used in this specification, specify the presence of stated features, regions, integers, steps, operations, elements, and/or components, but do not preclude the presence or addition of one or more other features, regions, integers, steps, operations, elements, components, and/or groups thereof.

Various embodiments of the present invention are disclosed in the accompanying drawings, and for purposes of clarity, numerous practical details are set forth in the following description. However, it should be understood that these practical details are not to be construed as limiting the present disclosure. That is, in some embodiments of the present disclosure, these practical details are unnecessary. In addition, for the sake of simplicity of the drawing, some of the conventional structures and elements are shown in the drawing in a simplified schematic manner.

FIG. 1 is a schematic diagram of a detection system 100 according to some embodiments of the present disclosure. In various embodiments, the detection system 100 may be provided on a variety of devices having detection requirements, such as an electric vehicle.

As shown in fig. 1, the detection system 100 includes sensors 110, 120, 130 and a processor 140. The sensor 110 is used for sensing the ambient environment SE1 to generate the sensing data SD11. The sensor 120 is used for sensing the surrounding environment SE1 to generate the sensing data SD12. The sensor 130 is used for sensing the ambient environment SE1 to generate the sensing data SD13. The processor 140 detects the ambient environment SE1 according to the sensing data SD 11-SD 13 and identifies objects and corresponding positions in the ambient environment SE 1.

In some embodiments, sensors 110, 120, and 130 are different types of sensors. For example, the sensors 110, 120, and 130 may be optical Radar (Light Detection AND RANGING, LIDAR), camera (camera), and Radar (Radar), respectively. In the above example, the sensing data SD11 and SD13 are three-dimensional data, and the sensing data SD12 is two-dimensional data.

In the embodiment shown in fig. 1, detection system 100 includes three sensors 110, 120, and 130, but embodiments of the present disclosure are not limited thereto. In various embodiments, the detection system 100 may include various numbers and types of sensors.

Fig. 2 is a flow chart of a machine learning method 200 according to some embodiments of the present disclosure. In some embodiments, the machine learning method 200 may be performed by the processor 140 shown in fig. 1, but the embodiments of the present disclosure are not limited thereto. In various embodiments, machine learning method 200 may also be performed by various processors other than processor 140.

In some embodiments, the machine learning method 200 is used to generate the prediction data PD21 according to the sensing data SD21 and SD 22. The sensing data SD21 and SD22 correspond to different kinds of sensors. For example, the sensing data SD21 and SD22 correspond to the sensors 110 and 120 shown in fig. 1, respectively.

During training, the sensing data SD21 and SD22 may be data in a database. In practical applications, the sensing data SD21 and SD22 may be data sensed by a sensor, such as the sensing data SD11 and SD12 shown in fig. 1.

As shown in fig. 2, the machine learning method 200 includes operations OP21 to OP215. However, the embodiments of the present invention are not limited thereto. In different embodiments, machine learning method 200 may also perform various combinations of some or all of operations OP 21-OP 215 in various orders.

In operation OP21, the detector DT21 detects the objects OB1 to OB3 in the sensing data SD21 to generate the object data PL2. In some embodiments, the item data PL2 includes a confidence score (SCL 2) and a bounding box (BXL 2). The confidence score SCL2 may include confidence scores SCL 21-SCL 23 corresponding to the objects OB 1-OB 3, respectively. The bounding box BXL2 may contain bounding boxes BXL 21-BXL 23 corresponding to the objects OB 1-OB 3, respectively. The confidence scores SCL 21-SCL 23 correspond to probabilities that the classification model of the detector DT21 assigns the objects OB 1-OB 3 to a particular class (e.g., class of automobile), respectively. The bounding boxes BXL 21-BXL 23 correspond to the locations, volumes and orientations (headings) of the objects OB 1-OB 3 in the space of the sensing data SD21, respectively.

In operation OP22, the detector DT22 detects the objects OB1 to OB3 in the sensing data SD22 to generate the object data PI2. In some embodiments, the item data PI2 includes a confidence score SCI2 and a bounding box BXI2. The confidence score SCI2 may include confidence scores SCI 21-SCI 23 corresponding to the objects OB 1-OB 3, respectively. The bounding box BXI2 may contain bounding boxes BXI21 to BXI23 corresponding to the objects OB1 to OB3, respectively. The confidence scores SCI 21-SCI 23 correspond to the probabilities that the classification model of the detector DT22 assigns the objects OB 1-OB 3 to a particular class (e.g., class of automobile), respectively. The bounding boxes BXI 21-BXI 23 correspond to the positions and the volumes of the objects OB 1-OB 3 in the space of the sensing data SD22, respectively.

Referring to fig. 1 and 2, the detector DT21 may correspond to one of the sensors 110, 120, and 130, and the detector DT22 may correspond to the other of the sensors 110, 120, and 130. For example, detectors DT21 and DT22 may correspond to optical radars and cameras, respectively. In the above example, the sensing data SD21 is optical radar point cloud (point cloud) data, which corresponds to the data sensed by the sensor 110 as an optical radar, and the sensing data SD22 is red-green-blue (RGB) image data, which corresponds to the data sensed by the sensor 120 as a camera. In some embodiments, each of detectors DT21 and DT22 may be implemented by a convolutional neural network (Convolution Neural Network).

In some embodiments, the sensing data SD21 and SD22 correspond to the same ambient environment, such as the ambient environment SE1 shown in fig. 1. Correspondingly, each of the sense data SD21 and SD22 has data of the objects OB 1-OB 3 in the ambient environment SE1. In the embodiment shown in fig. 2, the sensing data SD21 and SD22 have three objects OB1 to OB3, but the embodiment of the disclosure is not limited thereto. In various embodiments, the sensing data SD21 and SD22 may include various numbers of objects. Correspondingly, the detectors DT21 and DT22 may generate various amounts of object data.

In operation OP23, the processor maps (project) object data corresponding to the same object (e.g., one of the objects OB 1-OB 3) from among the object data PL2 and PI 2.

In operation OP25, the processor generates uncertainty scores (uncertainty score) ULC2 and ULB2 corresponding to the object data PL2 according to the sensing data SD 21. In some embodiments, the uncertainty score ULC2 is the uncertainty score of the confidence score SCL2, and the uncertainty score ULB2 is the uncertainty score of the bounding box BXL 2. Details regarding operation OP25 are further described below in connection with the embodiment of fig. 3A.

In operation OP24, the processor generates uncertainty scores (uncertainty score) UIC2 and UIB2 corresponding to the object data PI2 according to the sensing data SD 22. In some embodiments, uncertainty score UIC2 is the uncertainty score of confidence score SCI2, and uncertainty score UIB is the uncertainty score of bounding box BXI 2. Details regarding operation OP24 are further described below in connection with the embodiment of fig. 3B.

At operation OP26, the processor inputs at least a portion of the item data PI2 (e.g., the confidence score SCI 2) and the uncertainty scores UIC2, UIB2 into the model MD1.

At operation OP27, the processor inputs at least a portion of the item data PL2 (e.g., confidence score SCL 2) and uncertainty scores ULC2, ULB2 into the model MD1.

As shown in fig. 2, the hybrid model MD1 may be a hybrid Expert fusion model based on uncertainty coding, which includes Expert networks (ENL 2, ENI2 and Gating networks (Gating networks) GNL2, GNI2.

In some embodiments, expert networks ENL2 and ENI2 correspond to detectors DT21 and DT22, respectively. For example, when the detector DT21 corresponds to an optical radar, the expert network ENL2 is an optical radar expert network and is used for training according to a database of the corresponding optical radar. When the detector DT22 corresponds to a camera, the expert network ENL2 is a camera expert network and is used for training according to the database of the corresponding camera.

As shown in FIG. 2, model MD1 is used to encode uncertainty scores UIC2, UIB2, ULC2, and ULB2 to generate weight data WL2 and WI2. Correspondingly, in some embodiments, the model MD1 is referred to as an Uncertainty-encoded hybrid expert fusion module (Uncertitry-encoded Mixture-of-Experts fusion module).

In operation OP28, the expert network ENI2 generates feature data FI2 according to the confidence score SCI2 and the uncertainty scores UIC2, UIB 2.

In operation OP29, the expert network ENL2 generates the feature data FL2 according to the confidence score SCL2 and the uncertainty scores ULC2, ULB 2.

In operation OP210, the processor generates Joint Feature (Joint Feature) data FJ2 from the Feature data FI2 and FL 2. In some embodiments, the joint feature data FJ2 includes information for confidence scores SCI2, SCL2 and uncertainty scores UIC2, UIB2, ULC2, ULB 2.

In operation OP211, the gating network GNL2 generates weight data WL2 according to the joint feature data FJ 2.

In operation OP212, the gating network GNI2 generates weight data WI2 according to the joint feature data FJ 2.

In operation OP213, the processor inputs the item data PL2 and the weight data WL2 into the fusion network FN2.

In operation OP214, the processor inputs the object data PI2 and the weight data WI2 into the fusion network FN2.

In operation OP215, the fusion network FN2 generates the prediction data PD21 according to the object data PL2, PI2 and the weight data WL2, WI 2. In some embodiments, the prediction data PD21 includes predicted locations and predicted categories of the objects OB 1-OB 3.

During training, the processor compares the predicted data PD21 with the actual data (e.g., the actual positions and the actual categories) of the objects OB 1-OB 3, and adjusts the parameters of the expert networks ENL2, ENI2, the gating networks GNL2, GNI2 and the fusion network FN2 according to the comparison result, so that the predicted data PD21 gradually approaches the actual data. For example, the processor generates a loss function according to the difference between the predicted data PD21 and the actual data, and trains the expert networks ENL2, ENI2, the gating networks GNL2, GNI2, and the fusion network FN2 according to the loss function.

In practical applications, the processor may control the device to perform corresponding operations according to the prediction data PD21. For example, the processor may control the items OB1 to OB3 in the electric vehicle avoidance prediction data PD21.

In some implementations, when training the model, the model tends to make a too confident determination for the items in the adverse context (adverse scenario), i.e., the model easily classifies items of non-specific categories into specific categories to produce a false positive determination. In addition, when fusing object data of different sensors, some sensors are highly affected by adverse situations, and the processor equally considers all object data, so that the model performs poorly.

In contrast to the above, in the embodiment of the present invention, the processor generates uncertainty scores ULC2, ULB2, UIC2 and UIB2 corresponding to the different sensors 110 and 120 through the different types of detectors DT21 and DT22, and trains the model MD1 through the uncertainty scores ULC2, ULB2, UIC2 and UIB. In adverse situations, the uncertainty score is higher. In this way, the processor can consider the influence of the adverse situation and train the model MD1, so that the model MD1 performs better.

Fig. 3A is a flowchart illustrating further details of the operation OP25 shown in fig. 2 according to some embodiments of the present disclosure. As shown in fig. 3A, the operations OP25 may include operations OP31 to OP33.

At operation OP31, the processor turns on the drop out (drop out) layer in the detector DT 21. In some embodiments, the operation of opening the drop layer in operation OP31 is a step of a monte carlo drop operation.

In operation OP32, the detector DT21 generates a plurality of confidence scores SCL3 and a plurality of bounding boxes BXL3 according to the sensing data SD 21. For example, the processor inputs the sensing data SD21 into the detector DT21 multiple times, and the detector DT21 correspondingly outputs one of the multiple confidence scores SCL3 at each input.

In operation OP33, the processor calculates an uncertainty score ULC2 from the plurality of confidence scores SCL3 and an uncertainty score ULB2 from the plurality of bounding boxes BXL 3. Specifically, the uncertainty score ULC2 is greater when the distribution of the plurality of confidence scores SCL3 is wider. The uncertainty fraction ULB2 is greater when the distribution of the bounding box BXL3 is wider.

Fig. 3B is a flowchart illustrating further details of the operation OP24 shown in fig. 2 according to some embodiments of the present disclosure. As shown in fig. 3B, operations OP24 may include operations OP 34-OP 36.

At operation OP34, the processor turns on the drop out (drop out) layer in the detector DT 22.

In operation OP35, the detector DT22 generates a plurality of confidence scores SCI3 and a plurality of bounding boxes BXI3 according to the sensing data SD 22. For example, the processor inputs the sensing data SD22 into the detector DT22 a plurality of times, and the detector DT22 outputs one of a plurality of confidence scores SCI3 corresponding to each input.

In operation OP36, the processor calculates an uncertainty score UIC2 from the plurality of confidence scores SCI3 and an uncertainty score UIB2 from the plurality of bounding boxes BXI 3. Specifically, the uncertainty score UIC2 is larger as the distribution of the plurality of confidence scores SCI3 is wider. The greater the uncertainty score UIB2, the wider the distribution of the bounding box BXI 3.

Fig. 4 is a flow chart of a machine learning method 400 according to some embodiments of the present disclosure. In some embodiments, the machine learning method 400 may be performed by the processor 140 shown in fig. 1, but the embodiments of the present disclosure are not limited thereto. In various embodiments, the machine learning method 400 may also be performed by various processors other than the processor 140.

Referring to fig. 4 and 2, a machine learning method 400 is a variation of the machine learning method 200. Therefore, for the sake of brevity, some details will not be repeated. In comparison to the machine learning method 200, the machine learning method 400 further includes operations OP 41-OP 44.

In operation OP41, the detector DT41 detects the objects OB1 to OB3 in the sensing data SD41 to generate the object data PR4. In some embodiments, the item data PR4 includes a confidence score SCR4 and a bounding box BXR4. The confidence scores SCR4 may include confidence scores SCR 41-SCR 43 corresponding to the objects OB 1-OB 3, respectively. The bounding box BXR may contain bounding boxes BXR-BXR 43 corresponding to the objects OB 1-OB 3, respectively. The confidence scores SCR 41-SCR 43 correspond to probabilities that the classification model of the detector DT41 assigns the objects OB 1-OB 3 to a particular class (e.g., class of automobile), respectively. The bounding boxes BXR-BXR 43 correspond to the locations and volumes of the objects OB 1-OB 3, respectively, in the space of the sensing data SD 41.

Referring to fig. 1 and 4, the detector DT41 may correspond to one of the sensors 110, 120, and 130. For example, the detector DT41 may correspond to a radar. In the above example, the sensing data SD41 is radar point cloud data, i.e., data sensed by the sensor 130 corresponding to radar. In some embodiments, the detector DT41 may be implemented by a convolutional neural network (Convolution Neural Network).

In some embodiments, the sensing data SD41 corresponds to the same ambient environment, such as the ambient environment SE1 shown in fig. 1. Correspondingly, the sensing data SD41 has data of the objects OB 1-OB 3 in the surrounding environment SE1. In the embodiment shown in fig. 4, the sensing data SD41 has three objects OB1 to OB3, but the embodiment of the disclosure is not limited thereto. In various embodiments, the sensing data SD41 may include various numbers of items. Correspondingly, the detector DT41 may generate various amounts of object data.

In operation OP42, the processor generates uncertainty scores URC4 and URB4 corresponding to the object data PR4 according to the sensing data SD 41. In some embodiments, the uncertainty score URC4 is the uncertainty score of the confidence score SCR4, and the uncertainty score URB4 is the uncertainty score of the bounding box BXR 4.

Referring to fig. 3A, 3B and 4, in some embodiments, the operations OP42 may include operations similar to those of OPs 31-36. Therefore, for brevity, some descriptions will not be repeated.

At operation OP43, the processor inputs at least a portion of the object data PR4 (e.g., the confidence score SCR 4) and the uncertainty scores URC4, URB4 into the model MD1.

In the embodiment shown in fig. 4, the model MD1 also contains an expert network ENR4. The expert network ENR4 corresponds to the detector DT41. For example, when the detector DT41 corresponds to an optical radar, the expert network ENR4 is a radar expert network and is used for training according to a database of the corresponding radar.

In operation OP44, the expert network ENR4 generates the feature data FR4 according to the confidence score SCR4 and the uncertainty scores URC4, URB 4.

In the embodiment shown in fig. 4, the processor generates joint feature data FJ2 according to the feature data FR4, FI2, and FL2 in operation OP 210. Correspondingly, the weight data WL2 and WI2 include information of the feature data FR 4. In this way, the prediction data PD21 generated by training the weight data WL2 and WI2 includes the information of the uncertainty scores URC4, URB4, so that the prediction accuracy is increased.

As shown in fig. 4, in some embodiments, the machine learning method 400 may further include operations OP 45-OP 46, and the model MD1 may further include a gating network GNR4.

In operation OP45, the gating network GNR4 generates weight data WR4 according to the joint feature data FJ 2.

In operation OP46, the processor inputs the object data PR4 and the weight data WR4 into the fusion network FN2.

In the embodiment shown in fig. 4, in operation OP215, the fusion network FN2 generates the prediction data PD21 according to the object data PL2, PI2, PR4 and the weight data WL2, WI2, WR 4.

Fig. 5 is a flow chart of a machine learning method 500 according to some embodiments of the present disclosure. In some embodiments, the machine learning method 500 may be performed by the processor 140 shown in fig. 1, but the present disclosure embodiments are not so limited. In various embodiments, the machine learning method 500 may also be performed by various processors other than the processor 140.

As shown in fig. 5, the machine learning method 500 includes operations OP51 to OP54. In operation OP51, the neural network NN1 generates object data and corresponding uncertainty scores and inputs the model MD1. In operation OP52, the neural network NN2 generates object data and corresponding uncertainty scores and inputs the model MD1. In operation OP53, the neural network NN3 generates object data and corresponding uncertainty scores and inputs the model MD1. In various embodiments, the machine learning method 500 may generate the item data and corresponding uncertainty scores through various numbers of neural networks and input the model MD1.

In operation OP54, the model MD1 generates weight data W5 according to the object data of the neural networks NN1 to NN3 and the corresponding uncertainty score to train the model MD 1.

Referring to fig. 5 and 4, a machine learning method 500 is a variation of the machine learning method 400. The neural networks NN 1-NN 3 correspond to the detectors DT21, DT22 and DT41, respectively. The weight data W5 corresponds to the weight data WL2, WI2, and WR4. Therefore, for the sake of brevity, some details will not be repeated.

In various embodiments, the neural networks NN 1-NN 3 may correspond to various types of detectors, transducers (transducers), or neural networks that correspond to other tasks.

Although the present invention has been described with reference to the above embodiments, it should be understood that the invention is not limited thereto, but rather may be modified or altered somewhat by persons skilled in the art without departing from the spirit and scope of the present invention.
